topic: How can dynamic power allocation balance network efficiency and outage probability in multibeam satellite payloads with phase noise?
consensus_response: Dynamic power allocation balances network efficiency and outage probability by optimizing the trade-off between used power and satisfaction index (ASI) in multibeam satellite payloads with phase noise. Phase noise degrades SNR, increasing BER, while inter-beam interference (IBI) is exacerbated by phase noise, requiring mitigation techniques such as adaptive beamforming or frequency-domain equalization. Non-linear effects from high-power amplifiers cause intermodulation distortion, further degrading system performance. Cognitive radio and machine learning can adapt transmission parameters based on channel conditions, optimizing power allocation and reducing interference. By minimizing average unmet system capacity (AUSC) and maximizing ASI, dynamic power allocation can balance network efficiency and outage probability.
